selected_evidence.summary: Shows root:root ownership, mode 1777, and successful file creation by both `antrieb` and `nobody`.

selected_evidence.requirement: Users cannot remove files owned by other users
selected_evidence.summary: Before and after restart, `nobody` received `Operation not permitted` when deleting an `antrieb`-owned file, and the file remained present.
Captures the healthy pre-restart directory and data state, original boot ID, and acknowledged native reboot scheduling.
Shows the new boot ID `ca34e366-28b9-43b2-b36c-bec237507bac` with five seconds uptime.
Directly compares old and new boot IDs and proves recovered mode 1777, writable filesystem, persisted data, sticky-bit enforcement, and final cleanup.

commands.command:
set -eu
printf 'boot_id='; cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id
printf 'node='; hostname
printf 'directory='; if [ -e /srv/drop ]; then stat -c '%F %U:%G %a %A %n' /srv/drop; else echo absent; fi

commands.command:
set -eu
owner_file=/srv/drop/.sticky-owner-test
other_file=/srv/drop/.sticky-other-test
rm -f "$owner_file" "$other_file"
printf 'owned by antrieb\n' > "$owner_file"
sudo -u nobody sh -c 'printf "owned by nobody\n" > /srv/drop/.sticky-other-test'
printf 'write_proof:\n'
stat -c '%U:%G %a %n' "$owner_file" "$other_file"
printf 'cross_owner_delete=' 
if sudo -u nobody rm "$owner_file" 2>/tmp/sticky-rm.err; then echo UNEXPECTED_SUCCESS; exit 1; else echo denied; fi
printf 'delete_error='; cat /tmp/sticky-rm.err
[ -f "$owner_file" ]
echo owner_file_preserved=yes
rm -f "$owner_file"
sudo -u nobody rm "$other_file"
rm -f /tmp/sticky-rm.err
echo cleanup=complete
stat -c 'directory_mode=%a directory_perms=%A owner=%U:%G path=%n' /srv/drop
commands.stdout:
write_proof:
antrieb:antrieb 664 /srv/drop/.sticky-owner-test
nobody:nogroup 644 /srv/drop/.sticky-other-test
cross_owner_delete=denied
delete_error=rm: cannot remove '/srv/drop/.sticky-owner-test': Operation not permitted
owner_file_preserved=yes
cleanup=complete
directory_mode=1777 directory_perms=drwxrwxrwt owner=root:root path=/srv/drop

commands.command:
set -eu
old_boot_id=a59a9d9a-a5e0-44f7-9ca1-7f28483971e0
new_boot_id=$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id)
printf 'old_boot_id=%s\nnew_boot_id=%s\n' "$old_boot_id" "$new_boot_id"
[ "$new_boot_id" != "$old_boot_id" ]
echo boot_id_changed=yes
printf 'directory='; stat -c '%U:%G %a %A %n' /srv/drop
printf 'filesystem='; findmnt -T /srv/drop -n -o TARGET,SOURCE,FSTYPE,OPTIONS
printf 'persisted_data='; cat /srv/drop/.restart-persistence-check
owner_file=/srv/drop/.post-reboot-owner-test
rm -f "$owner_file"
printf 'post-reboot sticky test\n' > "$owner_file"
printf 'post_reboot_write='; stat -c '%U:%G %a %n' "$owner_file"
printf 'post_reboot_cross_owner_delete='
if sudo -u nobody rm "$owner_file" 2>/tmp/post-reboot-rm.err; then echo UNEXPECTED_SUCCESS; exit 1; else echo denied; fi
printf 'delete_error='; cat /tmp/post-reboot-rm.err
[ -f "$owner_file" ]
echo owner_file_preserved=yes
rm -f "$owner_file" /srv/drop/.restart-persistence-check /tmp/post-reboot-rm.err
echo verification_cleanup=complete
printf 'final_directory='; stat -c '%U:%G %a %A %n' /srv/drop
